stem:
Irfan estimates how many heartbeats a person has in one year. He takes about $70$ beats each minute.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: The yearly total is the word "estimate".
The length of one year is what produces the rate of $70$ beats each minute.
A close estimate is about $70 \times 60 \times 24 \times 365$ beats from the rate and the time factors.
Add $70+60+24+365$ to get the yearly number of beats.

teacher.key_rationale: Model beats/minute × minutes/hour × hours/day × days/year for a close estimate. Naming "estimate", reversing year into the rate, or adding the factors all miss the modeling hinge.
